---
title: "Errors"
---

```{python}
#| label: setup-errors
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Setup: the imports every example on this page uses"
#| output: false
import dataframely as dy
import polars as pl

import dagster_dataframely as dd
from dagster_dataframely.data import OrdersSchema, storefront_orders
```

Every error this package defines is in `dd.errors` and subclasses `dd.errors.DagsterDataframelyError`.
Catch one by name, or catch `DagsterDataframelyError` to catch every one.
Every message names what failed and what to do.

| error | raised | what to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CollectionNotSupportedError` | when you declare the asset | pass a `dy.Schema`; declare one asset per Collection member, each with the member's own schema, then pass them to `dd.build_collection_checks` |
| `InvalidMembersError` | when `dd.build_collection_checks` is called | map every required member, and only the Collection's members, to an unpartitioned asset; the message lists the members |
| `FailurePropagationError` | when `dd.build_collection_checks` is called | remove `propagate_row_failures=True` from the member, or write a collection filter that states the condition |
| `ReservedColumnError` | when you declare the asset, and by every public function that takes a schema except `dd.wiring.get_code_version` | rename the column that starts with `dy_` |
| `InvalidColumnNameError` | when you declare the asset, and by every public function that takes a schema except `dd.wiring.get_code_version` | rename the column, or change the `alias=` that sets its name, so the name uses only `A-Za-z0-9_`, the characters Dagster allows in a check name |
| `CheckNameCollisionError` | when you declare the asset, and by every public function that takes a schema except `dd.wiring.get_code_version` | rename one of the two rules that produce the same check name |
| `InvalidSeverityError` | when you declare the asset, by every public function that takes a schema, and when `dd.build_collection_checks` is called | fix the severity declaration the message names; [Rule severity](rule-severity.qmd) lists the forms, and [Collection checks](collection-checks.qmd#severity) covers a Collection's |
| `InvalidSettingError` | when you declare the asset, or when another function that reads the setting is called | fix the value at the source the message names |
| `MaterializeResultValueError` | before the column-schema check | set `value=` to the frame; or return the frame and call `context.add_asset_metadata`; or write a plain `@dg.asset` and call `dd.wiring.get_column_schema_metadata`; to skip, return `None` itself |
| `MaterializeResultFieldError` | before the column-schema check | remove `asset_key=` or `check_results=`, which the decorator sets itself |
| `ColumnSchemaError` | after the column-schema check fails | fix the function that produced the frame, or cast with `Schema.cast` in the asset body; for `dd.build_rule_checks`, declare the dtype the table stores, or change what writes the table |
| `ValidationAbortError` | after `Schema.filter`, when a row failed an `"error"` rule and the asset has `filter=False` | fix the rows upstream, write them under `<name>__error_rows` with `filter=True`, declare the rule `"warn"`, or drop them in the asset body |
| `NoValidRowsError` | after `Schema.filter`, when every row failed an `"error"` rule and the asset has `filter=True` | read the error rows at the address in the message, then fix the rows upstream or declare the rule `"warn"` |
| `ErrorRowsKeyCollisionError` | before the decorated function runs, on every run of an asset with `filter=True` | rename the other asset, set `error_rows_key` to another key, or remove `filter=True`; if the other asset is your own table for the error rows, delete it and use `build_error_rows_spec` |
| `ErrorRowsDirError` | under direct invocation only, when there are error rows to write | set `DAGSTER_DATAFRAMELY_ERROR_ROWS_DIR`, or run the asset |

The package also raises Dagster's own errors in three cases.
`dd.asset` raises `dg.DagsterInvalidDefinitionError` when you declare the asset, if `error_rows_key` or `error_rows_io_manager_key` is set and `filter` is `False`.
When the decorated function returns anything other than a Polars frame, a `dg.MaterializeResult` or `None`, the run raises `dg.DagsterInvariantViolationError` before the column-schema check.
`build_error_rows_spec` raises `dg.DagsterInvariantViolationError` when it receives both an asset definition and a `partitions_def`.

`ColumnSchemaError` names every mismatched column at once, with its expected and actual dtype.
The failing check's `dataframely/column_schema_errors` table lists the same columns.

![A run log where the `quantity` column is `Int64`. The failing `dy_schema__columns` check has `dataframely/column_schema_errors`, which shows the expected and actual dtype. The step failure below it names the same column in the `ColumnSchemaError` message.](../assets/images/error-column-schema.png)

`ValidationAbortError` and `NoValidRowsError` both give the failure count per `"error"` rule.
The counts can add up to more than the number of failing rows, because one row can fail several rules.
When every row fails only `"warn"` rules, the run raises neither error and writes every row.

## Common mistakes

For each of these mistakes, the cause is not on the line where the traceback ends.

**Do not define another asset that materializes `<name>__error_rows` if `<name>` has `filter=True`.**
`orders` with `filter=True` writes its error rows to the asset key `orders__error_rows`, through the same IO manager that writes `orders`.
An asset of your own keyed `orders__error_rows` has the same address.
Both assets would write to the same table or file, and the second write would replace the first.
So every run of `orders` checks for such an asset before the decorated function runs, and raises:

```text
ErrorRowsKeyCollisionError: 'orders' declares `filter=True`, so its error rows are written to
'orders__error_rows', which an asset in this code location already materializes. Rename that asset,
set `error_rows_key` on 'orders' to another key, or remove `filter=True` from 'orders'. If that asset
is your own table for the error rows, delete it and use `build_error_rows_spec` instead, which adds the
error rows themselves to the asset graph.
```

With `error_rows_key`, the run checks that key instead.
The run also raises when that key is the asset's own key.

**With `from __future__ import annotations` in your module, Dagster raises for an annotated `context` parameter.**
Under PEP 563, Dagster receives every annotation as a string.
Dagster compares the `context` annotation with the real classes, so it raises this error for both `context: dg.AssetExecutionContext` and `context: AssetExecutionContext`:

```text
DagsterInvalidDefinitionError: Cannot annotate `context` parameter with type dg.AssetExecutionContext.
`context` must be annotated with AssetExecutionContext, AssetCheckExecutionContext, OpExecutionContext, or left blank.
```

`@dg.asset` raises the same error for the same annotation.
Both accept an unannotated `context`, which is the only option in that message that still works under PEP 563:

```{python}
#| label: errors-1
@dd.asset(OrdersSchema)
def orders(context) -> pl.DataFrame:
    context.log.info("run %s", context.run_id)
    return storefront_orders
```

**A `@dy.rule()` body needs its class parameter.**
Without it, Python still defines the schema class.
`dd.asset` reads the rule's expression when you declare the asset, and raises:

```text
TypeError: GiftOrdersSchema.gifts_have_priority() takes 0 positional arguments but 1 was given
```

Dataframely calls the body with the schema class, so the body takes `cls`:

```{python}
#| label: errors-2
class GiftOrdersSchema(OrdersSchema):
    @dy.rule()
    def gifts_have_priority(cls) -> pl.Expr:
        """Require a priority on a gift line."""
        return ~cls.is_gift.col | cls.priority.col.is_not_null()
```
